title: Resident Assistant
description: I am currently serving as a resident assistant for my dorm, Sorin College, to about 160 or so university men. I love this community, and so I am excited to learn many new faces and grow with the guys as best I can.

title: Software Engineering Intern
description: Software engineering internship for the memory forensics company Volexity, Inc. that took place in Silver Spring, MD. After some initial bootstrapping, I developed a feature for Surge, their flagship memory collection tool, that collects file birth times on Linux file systems when available using the statx system call. Beyond that initial project, I fixed a longstanding timestamp rounding bug in the testing architecture and researched the debuginfod protocol to expand debug symbol collection for various Linux kernels. The internship was also a fun time; kayaking and hiking with my coworkers were some highlights.

employer: IRES 2025 Research Program in Lyon, France
title: Undergraduate Researcher
description: Research internship under Dr. Michael Niemier in Lyon, France at École Centrale de Lyon. With 4 undergrads, I benchmarked figures of merit for AES hardware accelerators from 11+ research papers to compare to an in-development AES chip. I generated graphs via Python and Google Colab which were shown off in sponsor presentations. We additionally researched applying ferroelectrics to an AES accelerator through a modified bitcell using 1FeFET-1C cells for the SubBytes step of encryption. Beyond the research, being in France for two months was an incredible opportunity to engage with international students and eat pain au chocolat.

title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
description: In Fall of 2024, I was a teaching assistant for Discrete Mathematics for about 50 students. In Spring 2025, I was a grader for Magic of Numbers, a mathematics seminar for about fifteen first-year students. For Fall 2025, I was a Fundamentals of Computing TA for about 100 students. Fall 2026, I will be an Operating Systems TA.

title: Conversations of Purpose Mentor
description: The Foundations of Theology class I took included a weekly conversation with members of the same dorm. I served as a co-lead for these conversations with the members of Sorin College, my university dorm, fostering conversations about theology, faith, and the ways they relate to personal life for six first-years.

title: Radio and Communications Lead and Club Member
description: Domer Rover is an engineering club where our goal is to build a rover for the University Rover Competition. I served as the Radio and Communications Lead, teaching myself radios, earning a Technician-level Ham radio license (callsign KE9AZR), and developing a concurrent communication protocol between the rover and our base station that functions over two frequency bands. I designed the system to be message-based with handshakes to accomodate potential dips in communication. The system sends photos, driving controls, status signals, and video at a distance, and in testing worked at distances over a kilometer! Check out our SAR video embedded here to hear me talk about it.

title: Senior Staff
description: At Kilwins, the main ice cream and chocolate store near me, I provided friendly service, welcoming each customer at the door, offering samples of fudge, and helping them out with whatever they needed. I collaborated with my coworkers to serve lines of 100+ people for ice cream nearly every summer weekend, and I consistently worked about 25 hours/week in the summer and during all breaks. I also helped train a few new hires.
